newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Oct 2.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Oct 2.

text.p: AT&T Corp is set to launch a new service that brings together voice, data, paging and electronic mail in a cellular telephone that will reach 40 markets covering more than 70 million people, the Wall Street Journal reported Wednesday.
* Microsoft Corp will let an industry group called Open Group of Cambridge, Mass direct the evolution of the Internet technology that the company spent $100 million to develop.
* General Motors Corp is coming close to reaching a new labor contract agreement with union leaders.

* Foundation Health Corp and Health Systems International Inc have signed a definitive agreement for a stock-swap merger worth $2.3 billion. The new company will have 1997 revenues totalling more than $8 billion.
* Chrysler Corp car and light truck sales rose 22 percent in September, while General Motors Corp combined sales shrunk 2.2 percent for the same period.
* The index of leading U.S. economic indicators rose 2.0 percent in August. A report on manufacturing showed moderate growth in September.
* East Coast dockworkers are voting on a contract that could save shippers money .
* Grigsby Brandford's two last partners joined Muriel Siebert amid a federal inquiry into the bond firm's former chief executive officer Calvin Grigsby.
* United Steelworkers went on strike at WHX Corp 's Wheeling-Pittsburgh following disagreements over a pension proposal.
* U.S. Food and Drug Administration approved Eli Lilly & Co's anti-psychotic drug Zyprexa.
* U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission is expected to close its probe into a bond offering for the Denver International Airport without taking any action against it.
* Mark IV is expected to cut 1,000 employees and take a $110 million pre-tax charge.

* Bond prices rose following signs that the manufacturing sector grew at a moderate rate in September. They also got support from published remarks by U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan about his optimistic outlook on inflation.

* Some mutual funds have sold their stock in restaurant chain Planet Hollywood International Inc because they are not willing to run the risk of growing competition, faltering revenues at restaurants open more than a year and the possibility of market saturation for more Planet Hollywood outlets.
